title: Hunters and sorcerers
summary: What the imbued make of people who bend reality.

claims.text: Wizards and witches live everywhere, from huts to modern Western cities, shopping and walking the streets like anyone while able to bend minds, bodies and chance.

Hunters who see such people work their miracles wonder whether old witch-hunts had a point, but know little beyond legend: whether witches eat children, deal with demons or cloud the minds of officials and governments.
Hunters find sorcerers on the streets, at universities and in posts of authority, and guess that those they manage to stop are the least experienced of their kind.

title: Faces of the spellbound
summary: How hunters and sorcerers look to one another.

claims.text: Hunters and mages can be so alike in body and spirit that neither can always tell one from the other.
Some sorcerers pursue strange realms and obsessions that border on madness, and some build cruel private worlds for themselves and their followers.
Some work magic through science, which forces hunters to ask whether their own ideal world is so different, and when science has gone too far.
To sorcerers, hunters are often baffling.
